title: Wexler as producer versus Wexler as person
summary: Matassa has no problem with Wexler's production work but objects to his behaviour toward history and thinks him not a nice person.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: So you didn't see Jerry as a great producer?
Oh, he was a good producer.
He was a very good producer.
Well, I don't have any problem with his work. I have any problem with his person.
Taking credit for things that maybe he didn't do.
Well, it wasn't so much like. Taking credit. But acting in this fashion that was totally inappropriate for what history was.

That sort of thing. And I think that's terrible. You know, I would hope I would never do a thing like that. And if I ever did it inadvertently, I hope some friend of mine would grab my foot and say, Are you crazy? You know, cut that out.
You know, because it's not a nice thing to do. Okay. So I don't think he's a nice person. Let's put it that way.
